mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, reflecting weakening economic activity and lower corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in GDPC1 over the same month signals a divergence between housing activity and overall economic output, suggesting a housing-led slowdown that precedes equity market underperformance over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND GDPC1 < previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS and a decrease in UNRATE over two months indicates a rise in employment but a fall in the unemployment rate, signaling labor market saturation and wage inflation, which compresses margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% for three consecutive months signals a risk of deflation, prompting anticipatory monetary easing, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both GDPC1 and RSAFS over three months indicates strengthening aggregate demand and corporate cash flow, which increases earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month AND RSAFS > previous month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
